summary: SpaceRelics is an interactive, web-based space heritage platform that brings the stories of NASA's forgotten space equipment to life. Since the 1960s, missions to the Moon, Mars and deep space have left behind landers, rovers, scientific instruments and spacecraft. Our platform transforms this forgotten hardware into an engaging digital learning experience through an interactive planetary explorer, searchable relic archive, mission timelines and an immersive Apollo 11 storytelling experience. Users can explore historic equipment, discover mission landing sites and understand the engineering principles behind propulsion, mobility, measurement and deep-space communication. By combining space history, science and interactive storytelling, SpaceRelics makes complex space exploration concepts accessible and engaging for school students and space enthusiasts. Our mission is to preserve the stories of these remarkable machines, highlight their scientific contributions and inspire the next generation of explorers, engineers and scientists.
details:
SpaceRelics is an interactive web-based space heritage museum designed to make the history of NASA's abandoned, inactive and still-operating space equipment accessible and engaging.

The platform organizes space relics into three exploration frontiers: the Moon, Mars and Deep Space. Users can browse a searchable relic archive, explore historical machines, understand their original missions and learn about their current status. Each relic includes information about its purpose, mission history and scientific contribution.

The platform offers several interactive learning features, including:
• Planetary Explorer: Explore mission landing sites on the Moon and Mars through an interactive map.
• Relic Archive: Discover historic landers, rovers, scientific instruments and spacecraft.
• Mission Timeline: Follow important milestones in human and robotic space exploration.
• Story Mode: Experience the Apollo 11 Eagle Lunar Module's journey through five storytelling chapters.
• Engineering Learning Zone: Understand propulsion, rover mobility, seismometers and deep-space communication.

Our solution transforms historical mission data into visual storytelling and interactive education. It aims to help students and space enthusiasts understand the engineering, science and legacy behind space exploration.

The intended impact is to preserve space heritage, improve scientific awareness and inspire future generations to explore STEM fields.
